passage.quote: The desktop reader is where a person explores that account of the program. They can read a description, move to a broader or more detailed explanation, inspect linked source alongside the prose, and see what a proposed change alters. The reader also shows recorded test outcomes and broken links while work is in progress.

from.quote: Descriptions can be read as short bullet summaries when a full account would interrupt orientation.

summary: Paired panes show a parent and active child together; implementation links place the owning description beside source.
Arrows navigate throughout the reader. The bottom menu shows nearby descriptions, and the tree overview exposes the whole hierarchy.

Each pane can switch independently to summary reading. View offers change highlighting and history. Tests accompany their descriptions and implementation; unfinished behavior and actual problems remain visible.
The desktop reads project content and reflects external edits; it neither edits nor accepts changes.
